exercise.name: Incline Bench Preacher Curl
library_steps: Stand behind an incline bench and drape one arm over the backrest.
Curl the dumbbell up with your upper arm pressed on the pad.
Lower slowly, finish your reps, then switch arms.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing behind a 60 deg back pad, armpit over its top edge, upper arm lying down the pad (shoulder flexed ~60 deg); palm up, the elbow goes from ~20 deg (nearly straight) to ~120 deg. Biceps is the target, with most effort near the stretched bottom.

setup.target: Back pad set steep (60 deg), athlete behind it, chest against the back of the pad, armpit hooked over the top edge.
setup.why: The pad fixes the upper arm in shoulder flexion, the defining preacher position; 60 deg lets a standing adult reach the top edge.

setup.target: Whole back of the upper arm flat on the pad, stays there.
setup.why: Biceps EMG peaked at 75 deg shoulder flexion in an isometric curl (S2).

setup.target: Supinated (palm up), one dumbbell; other hand rests on the pad.
setup.why: Library: one arm at a time.

setup.target: Feet hip-width behind the bench, knees soft, leaning into the pad.
setup.why: Gets the shoulder down to pad height.

movement.end: 120 deg (forearm ~60 deg above level, before vertical)

movement.measure: upper arm angle from the torso; stays still on the pad

muscles.emg: Preacher curl: ~80% of max RMS early in the lift, falling toward the top; higher than standing/incline curls in the first third, lower in the last third (S1). Shoulder flexion 75 deg gave the highest biceps EMG (115.6%) of 30-90 deg (S2).
flexor carpi radialis did not differ across shoulder angles (S2)

mistakes.mistake: Upper arm lifts off the pad
mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Elbow rises as the dumbbell comes up.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Library: upper arm pressed on the pad; shoulder takes over.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Arm snaps fully straight at the bottom.
mistakes.why_it_matters: The bottom is where preacher effort is highest; stop short of lockout (subjects started at ~20 deg).

sources.citation: Oliveira LF, Matta TT, Alves DS, Garcia MAC, Vieira TMM. 2009. Effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls. J Sports Sci Med 8:24-29.
sources.what_it_gave: Dumbbell preacher vs standing vs incline curl. Preacher: high biceps activity only near extension, lower in the top third; shorter ROM; reps began at ~20 deg elbow flexion.

sources.citation: Moon J, Shin I, Kang M, et al. 2013. The effect of shoulder flexion angles on the recruitment of upper-extremity muscles during isometric contraction. J Phys Ther Sci 25(10):1299-1301.
sources.what_it_gave: n=13 trained men, shoulder flexion 30-90 deg on a curl machine: biceps EMG and force peaked at 75 deg (115.6%).

clip_check.check: Upper arm lies on the pad in both pictures
Torso not inside the pad or strut
Feet flat on the floor behind the bench, clear of the bench foot
Palm up on the handle; free hand on the pad, no prop
Biceps strongest red in both pictures
